purpose: This tool lets you test a surprising rule: an angle made on the edge of a circle is always half the angle at the centre over the same arc. Move the points around and see the ratio never change.

stops.title: A circle with three points
stops.text: Drag A, B or P around the circle. The yellow arc is the arc AB that P does not sit on. The red lines and red number show the central angle at O. The green lines and green number show the inscribed angle at P.
stops.try: Drag P along the circle on the far side of AB. The green angle does not change.

stops.title: Point sliders
stops.text: These three sliders move A, B and P by angle around the circle, the same as dragging. Use them when you want exact positions, or on a touch screen.
stops.try: Set A and B 180 degrees apart. The inscribed angle becomes 90 degrees.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 shows the angle stays the same as P moves, and changes when P crosses the chord. Step 2 makes the arc 190 degrees. Step 3 sets A and B at opposite ends of a diameter for the right angle.

teacher: Ask students to predict the green angle before moving P, then check the readout ratio stays 2.00. Ask: what happens when P crosses to the other side of AB? Misconception: thinking the inscribed angle depends on where P sits on the arc. Project step 3 for Thales.
